newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A Taka 128 billion Annual Development Plan (ADP) for the coming 1997-98 fiscal year (July-June) was approved on Tuesday by the National Economic Council.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday approved the creation of a separate legislative drafting wing under the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs.
A $40 million project on dredging of the Goari river is likley to start in December to combat rising salinity in south-western districts.
Employees of Bangladesh's central secretariat on Wednesday begin one-hour work stoppage everyday for a week to protest the new office timing between 9 am and 5 pm.
The government has barred imports of 38 items under CRF (Clean Report of Findings), a facility that allows importers to take delivery of consignments without assessment by the customs authority.
Dissident leaders of Jatiya Party of former President Hussain Mohammad Ershad have called the council meeting on June 30.
Bangladesh's jute yarn and twine products are losing markets to Indian exports.
Bangladesh will receive $18.9 million in soft loan from the International Fund for Agriculture Development (IFAD). REUTER
